call_points.text: ₹1,728 Cr of a ₹2,000 Cr investment plan was committed till September 2026.
Cement capacity is planned to rise from 14.45 MTPA in FY25 to 17.55 MTPA by FY28.
Net debt rose to ₹1,591 Cr in September 2026 from ₹1,271 Cr in March 2026.
Green power (RE+WHRS) is planned to scale from 6% to 80% by FY29.
India Cements EBITDA per tonne rose to ₹603 this quarter from ₹386 in Q2FY26, improving every quarter.
India Cements revenue on a like-for-like ex-factory basis was ₹993 Cr, up 21%, on 19% volume growth.
About ₹2,000 Cr of cost-improvement capex is going into waste heat recovery and preheater/cooler upgrades at India Cements.
Green power at India Cements is to rise from about 3% of requirements to about 86% by end-FY28.
Merging India Cements into UltraTech awaits capex completion and non-core land disposal, targeted Q4FY28 or a quarter earlier.
Q2FY27 may look optically softer as monsoon slowdown and West Asia cost effects weigh on the quarter.
UltraTech targets double-digit grey cement volume growth for FY27.
UltraTech guides to ₹130-140 per tonne sequential cost increase in the July-September quarter.
UltraTech crossed 200 million tons of production capacity in India, becoming the largest cement company outside China.
Management expects sustainable volume growth of 7% to 8% per annum, supported by strong structural drivers in housing and infrastructure.

operating_notes.text: Scheme of amalgamation of four wholly owned Indian subsidiaries made effective from March 28, 2026.
Achieved domestic sales volume of 3.12 MnT in Q4FY26.
UltraTech crossed 200 million tons of production capacity in India in FY26.
India Cements EBITDA per tonne rose from about ₹386 in Q2FY26 to ₹603 in Q1FY27, per UltraTech's CFO.
India Cements revenue on a like-for-like ex-factory basis was ₹993 Cr in Q1FY27 versus ₹821 Cr, up 21% on 19% volume growth.
About ₹2,000 Cr of cost-improvement capex is being deployed at India Cements into waste heat recovery and preheater/cooler upgrades.
India Cements will invest up to ₹20.90 Cr for 3.62% of Zenataris Renewable Energy, an ISTS hybrid renewable SPV at Kudligi, Karnataka, supplying 11 MW to its cement plants on a group captive basis.
Zenataris reported turnover of ₹77.82 lakh in FY26 and nil in FY24 and FY25; it was incorporated on 9 October 2018.

timeline.summary: The India Cements reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,218 Cr and PAT of ₹60 Cr, alongside a ₹2,000 Cr capex plan.
Krishnagopal Ladsaria, CFO, disclosed the earnings call recording for Q4FY26 and FY26 on the company’s website.
The India Cements disclosed the transcript of UltraTech Cement's Q4 FY26 earnings call held on April 27, 2026.
The India Cements announced postal ballot voting results approving material related party transactions with holding company UltraTech Cement on 7 May 2026.
The India Cements received a compounding order from the RBI on May 15, 2026, paying a fee of ₹18,250 for a delayed Form FC-TRS filing.
On its 20 July 2026 Q1FY27 earnings call, UltraTech said India Cements' EBITDA per tonne had risen to ₹603 from ₹386 in Q2FY26 and kept the ₹1,000/t target, with full capex benefit from Q4FY28.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,142.03 Cr (+2.2% YoY), net profit ₹38.82 Cr (+340.6% YoY).
The India Cements Limited’s earnings call recording for Q2 and H1 FY2027, held on 1st October 2026, is available on the company’s website.
